newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela drains 165 bln bolivars with bank rule.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela drains 165 bln bolivars with bank rule.

text.p: A new ruling by Venezuela's Central Bank that ups reserve requirements to 15 percent will drain some 165 billion bolivars ($337 million) from the banking system, Central Bank president Antonio Casas Gonzalez said.

The ruling, published last week but effective Monday, forms part of the Central Bank's on-going efforts to mop up excess liquidity from the financial system and batten down against incipient inflationary pressures.
"We estimate that between 165 billion and 180 billion bolivars will be absorbed by the ruling, which is an important contribution to the Central Bank's efforts," Casas told reporters.

Casas said Venezuela's financial system last week held 400 billion bolivars more than the Central Bank deemed desirable, but he warned liquidity would continue to bubble up in coming weeks on pending payments by the government and state oil company PDVSA.
Under the ruling, commercial banks must now place 15 percent of the their deposits in non-interest bearing Central Bank accounts. The previous level was 12 percent.
According to a recent report by financial consultants Softline, total Venezuela bank deposits in May were 5.7 trillion bolivars ($11.8 billion).
